title: Quantile telemetry synthesis for POP selection and variant fallback
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Problem: We need a stable, production-safe way to pick a POP (region) and, if necessary, a lower-cost or compatible model variant when certain POPs degrade. Current routing uses raw p50/p95 windows independently and a separate network health gate; that has produced flip-flopping during short transients and poor decisions when latency percentiles diverge from network signals.

Goal: Build a single composite scoring pipeline that synthesizes p50/p95 latency quantiles with a lightweight network-health index (packet loss, 1m jitter, and tcp errors) into a normalized POP score. Use that score for primary POP election and for ranking safe fallback model variants (quantized / smaller-context variants) with hysteresis and cost-awareness.

High-level proposal:
1) Inputs: per-POP rolling p50 and p95 (30s/5m windows), per-POP network metrics (loss%, jitter_ms, tcp_errors_per_min), and recent traffic mix (percent streaming vs request-response).
2) Normalize each input to percentile-of-baseline using historical baseline per-POP and model-family. Baseline is EWMA with 1h half-life to allow diurnal shift but reduce noise.
3) Compose a composite score: S = w1*norm_p50 + w2*norm_p95 + w3*net_health_penalty + w4*cost_penalty.
   - net_health_penalty is an increasing function of packet loss and jitter with a guardrail that saturates at a configurable threshold (avoid over-penalizing noisy telemetry).
   - cost_penalty encodes model-variant unit cost delta (e.g., fp16 vs int8) so that cheaper variants are only favored when score delta is small.
4) Apply smoothing + hysteresis: turn-by-turn score EWMA (15s) and require a score gap > G and persistence T before switching primary POP. Provide immediate soft-failover option for read-only workloads.
5) Fallback ranking: produce an ordered list of compatible model variants per-POP by combining the composite score with a compatibility filter (tokenizer/arch match) and safety checks (latency SLA risk).

Acceptance criteria (see separate field): Composite scoring reduces POP churn by >40% on short spikes in internal perf tests and reduces tail latency regressions for fallbacks.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change cross-region data-plane routing protocols or alter billing. It only implements decisioning logic in the region selector service and exposes metrics for Console and Alerting.
acceptance_criteria: POP selection switches only after persistence T=30s and score gap G >= 12% (configurable) in staging experiments
Churn measured as POP-switches-per-minute drops >= 40% versus baseline on synthetic spike tests
Fallback variant ranking returns compatible variants ordered by composite score and shows correct cost_delta annotations
End-to-end latency p95 for canary traffic remains within SLA during a controlled pop degradation test
Metrics emitted: composite_score, norm_p50, norm_p95, net_health_penalty, cost_penalty, selected_variant, switch_reason
comments: 2026-03-10 Marco Chen: Initial triage + design sketch. Put together baseline normalization approach and draft weights. Leaving open questions on exact weight values and baseline half-life.

2026-03-11 Aisha Patel: Ran quick offline sim using last 30 days of telemetry (sample POPs). Early result: p95 dominant in 70% of degradations; network_loss spikes only explain 45% of routing deviations. Suggest w2(w_p95) >= w1(w_p50).

2026-03-11 Priya Rao (Perf): Perf harness shows EWMA half-life 1h is a reasonable compromise; try 1h/4h as A/B in canary. Also recommended a saturation cap on net_health_penalty at 0.6 to avoid full blackholing due to telemetry spikes.
2026-03-12 Aisha Patel: Opened draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/region-selector/pull/142. PR includes proto updates for composite_score and new metrics. Needs review from infra + telemetry.
2026-03-12 Security note (J. Morales): No customer data included. Forwarding to compliance to confirm no extra audit fields needed for private deployments.
